speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: They say at the Bell you make kings.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I make them and my fellows wear them.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: And there's a living in it?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There's a share in it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Ah. Then you're a carrier. You've only the one horse too many.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The share is the horse. When the door is shut, the share eats, and it does not pull.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Is the door shut?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The door is shut. I am walking home to a shut door. I am not bringing you a play to carry, and I am not bringing you the day it opens.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: A carrier who will not name the day is a carrier with a light load. I prefer it. Names get lost between Oxford and the Bell, and then a man pays me to carry the correction.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then carry this, and no correction. I do not wear the crown. A fellow wears it. I write the weight. I take a share of the door when the door is open.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: And when it is shut, you walk beside my horses and call the week a trade.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I call it the week. The trade is the share. The week is eleven pence, and a back that preferred the hill to the saddle.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Eleven pence. I heard the shape of you checking it. You did not tell me the rest. That is the first courteous thing you have done since Shipston.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The rest is not a story for an ale-bench. The eleven is the supper. The supper is bread and bacon. I have had it. I am still not a king.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Your fellows, you said. How many fellows does it take to wear one king?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Enough that you cannot point at a man in a yard and say, that one, he is the living. The living is the share. The man in the crown is a fellow, and he sweats the same as the rest.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Then I will not point. At the Bell they point. They like a trade they can tell in one breath to a man who has just got down.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let them tell it. You have the better sentence. One horse too many. I will keep that, and I will not improve it.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Don't. An improved sentence costs extra, and I am paid in miles.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Soft and steady, you said yesterday. A share can be slow. The man we passed could not.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: His horse said it for him. I am not saying it twice.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then once is the text. I make them. My fellows wear them. There is a share in it. You may tell the Bell that, if the Bell asks, and you may leave out the house.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: I was not offered the house. I was offered oats, and I answered oats. Sleep. Tomorrow is the last of the walking. You will be stiff in the first of it. I will not offer the spare unless you ask, and you will not ask.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not ask. If I am stiff, I will be stiff at your pace.

speaker: thomas_hobbins
text: Soft and steady still has the miles. A king who is only a share can afford to arrive late. We are not post.
